propositions: Push non-fast-forward recovery fails permanently when an untracked local file collides with a file the remote merge wants to create, leaving the untracked file in place and aborting the merge without self-healing.
The same untracked-overwrite collision class that reconverge recovers from (compaction leftovers: *-SNAPSHOT.json, *.retired) wedges push recovery because the abort path does not quarantine or retry.

After extending _recover_dirty_merge with quarantine-move-and-retry logic (parsing abort-named paths, moving untracked collisions to <git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/, and retrying the merge once), the push recovery completes with both parents and no bytes lost.
Tracked changes set aside in the stash commit object must be restored exactly once on every exit path (success, retry-failure, non-recoverable abort) to prevent loss of tracked edits.
Genuine merge conflicts (non-untracked-overwrite) and paths git does not name in the abort must keep today's abort-restore-warn behavior unchanged.
